A2.text:
Aysel loved her job at a marketing company in Baku, but she was very tired. Her workload was huge this month. She had a strict deadline for a new coffee shop project. She really wanted a promotion, so she worked late every evening.

Her colleague, Tural, sat next to her. Tural did not want to work in an office forever. He wanted to be an entrepreneur and open a small bookstore in Icherisheher.

One morning, Aysel showed her project to her boss, Leyla. Leyla looked at the papers and frowned. “This design is not right,” Leyla said. “We must start again. It is back to the drawing board.”

Aysel felt very sad. She wanted to resign and go home. She walked to the Boulevard and sat on a bench. Tural called her on the phone.

“Do not be sad,” Tural said. “Your ideas are great. You always work hard.”

The next day, Aysel went back to the office with a new idea. Leyla loved it. She smiled and gave Aysel the promotion. Leyla also gave her two days of remote work every week. Aysel was very happy. Tural smiled and brought her a cup of tea. It was a good day.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: Tural opening a new bookstore in Icherisheher
Aysel's hard work pays off after a difficult project
A boss who fires her employees
Why working in an office is bad
questions.why: Aysel works hard on a project, overcomes a failure, and finally gets a promotion and remote work.

questions.q: What did Tural want to do in the future?
options: Become the boss of the company
Be an entrepreneur and open a bookstore
questions.why: “He wanted to be an entrepreneur and open a small bookstore in Icherisheher.”

questions.q: Where did Aysel go when she felt sad?
questions.why: “She walked to the Boulevard and sat on a bench.”

questions.q: Leyla fired Aysel because the design was bad.
questions.why: Leyla did not fire her; she said they must start again, and later gave her a promotion.

questions.q: Leyla says, “It is back to the drawing board.” What does this mean?
options: To start again after something fails
To draw a picture of a board
To ask a colleague for help
questions.why: The design was not right, so they had to start the project again.

questions.q: How did Tural feel when Aysel came back with a new idea?
options: He was supportive and happy for her
He was jealous of her promotion
He was too busy to notice
questions.why: He called to encourage her earlier, and when she succeeded, he “smiled and brought her a cup of tea.”

B1.text:
Aysel worked at a busy marketing agency near Nizami Street in Baku. She liked her job, but recently her workload was impossible. She was trying to climb the ladder and get a much-needed promotion to Senior Designer. Because of a strict deadline for a major client, she stayed in the office until eight o'clock every night.

Her favorite colleague, Tural, had different plans for his future. He spent his weekends networking with local business owners. He dreamed of leaving the corporate world to become an entrepreneur and open an art café in Icherisheher.

On Wednesday, Aysel proudly presented her campaign to their manager, Leyla. Leyla looked at the slides in silence, sighed, and shook her head. “The client changed their mind about the colors yesterday,” she explained. “None of this works anymore. I am sorry, Aysel, but we are back to the drawing board.”

Aysel felt completely crushed. After weeks of hard work, she just wanted to resign and sleep for a month. She took a long walk along the Boulevard to clear her head, watching the ships on the Caspian Sea.

Later that evening, Tural sent her a message. “Don't give up,” he wrote. “You always go the extra mile for our clients. Just change the colors and keep your amazing concept.”

The next morning, Aysel presented the updated design. This time, Leyla was delighted. “This is perfect,” the manager said with a bright smile. “You handled the problem beautifully.” Not only did Aysel finally get her promotion, but Leyla also offered her two days of remote work each week so she could rest. Aysel smiled at Tural, knowing her hard work had finally paid off.

questions.q: Why did Aysel have to change her project?
options: Her manager did not like her attitude
The client changed their mind about the colors
questions.why: Leyla said, “The client changed their mind about the colors yesterday.”

questions.q: What did Tural do on the weekends?
options: He spent his time networking with local business owners
He studied to become a Senior Designer
He painted pictures at an art café
questions.why: “He spent his weekends networking with local business owners.”

questions.q: What did Leyla offer Aysel besides the promotion?
options: Two days of remote work each week
A new office on Nizami Street
A free vacation on the Caspian Sea
questions.why: “Leyla also offered her two days of remote work each week so she could rest.”

questions.q: Aysel finished her work early every day because she was fast.
questions.why: “She stayed in the office until eight o'clock every night.”

questions.q: Aysel was trying to “climb the ladder”. What does this phrase mean?
options: To leave the company and start a new business
To ask the boss for a longer deadline
To progress upward in your career
questions.why: She was trying to climb the ladder by getting a promotion to Senior Designer.

questions.q: Why did Aysel walk along the Boulevard?
options: She was meeting a major client there
She wanted to look for an art café
She needed to calm down after receiving bad news
questions.why: She felt completely crushed and wanted to clear her head.

B2.text:
Aysel had been working at a prestigious marketing agency in the heart of Baku for three years, and the pressure was finally getting to her. Her workload had doubled in the last quarter, largely because she was determined to climb the ladder and secure a highly competitive promotion to Art Director. With a brutal deadline approaching for their biggest client, she practically lived at her desk.

Her closest colleague, Tural, offered a sharp contrast to her corporate ambition. Tural spent his evenings attending industry events and networking with local investors. His ultimate goal was to resign from the agency, become an entrepreneur, and launch his own digital illustration studio in Icherisheher.

On Wednesday morning, Aysel presented her meticulously planned campaign to their demanding director, Leyla. Leyla stared at the vibrant slides for a long moment before letting out a heavy sigh. “The client sent an email at midnight,” Leyla said gently. “They are rebranding completely. The current concept is useless now. I'm afraid it is back to the drawing board.”

Aysel’s heart sank. She had sacrificed her weekends and evenings for this project. For a fleeting moment, she seriously considered packing her things and walking out of the building forever. To calm down, she grabbed her coat and took a brisk walk along the windy Boulevard, staring out at the grey waves of the Caspian Sea.

When she returned to her desk, there was a fresh cup of coffee and a sticky note from Tural waiting for her. “You always go the extra mile, and the clients know it. Don't let one email ruin your masterpiece. Tweak the core message and try again.”

Taking a deep breath, Aysel opened her laptop and spent the afternoon reshaping her original idea to fit the new brand guidelines. When she pitched the revised version the following morning, Leyla was genuinely impressed by her resilience.

“You handled that crisis brilliantly,” Leyla announced proudly. Not only did Aysel finally receive her hard-earned promotion, but the agency also transitioned her to a flexible remote work schedule. Sitting at a seaside café the next Monday, she realized the setback was exactly what she had needed.

questions.q: What is the main theme of the story?
options: The dangers of working too closely with friends
Overcoming a professional setback to achieve career success
How to start a digital illustration studio in Azerbaijan
Why remote work is bad for young professionals
questions.why: Aysel faces a major project failure, but perseveres and earns both a promotion and remote work.

questions.q: Why did the client's project need to be changed?
options: The client decided to rebrand completely
Tural gave Aysel the wrong information
questions.why: Leyla said, “They are rebranding completely. The current concept is useless now.”

questions.q: What did Tural leave on Aysel's desk to encourage her?
options: A fresh cup of coffee and a sticky note
A signed contract from a local investor
questions.why: “...there was a fresh cup of coffee and a sticky note from Tural waiting for her.”

questions.q: Tural wanted to stay at the agency and become the new Art Director.
questions.why: “His ultimate goal was to resign from the agency, become an entrepreneur, and launch his own digital illustration studio.”

questions.q: Tural writes, “You always go the extra mile.” What does this mean?
options: To walk a long distance to work
To do more than what is expected of you
questions.why: It means putting in extra effort beyond standard expectations, which she did by sacrificing her weekends.

questions.q: How did the remote work schedule change Aysel's perspective at the end?
options: It made her want to resign immediately
It helped her realize the stressful event had a positive outcome
It caused her to lose contact with Tural
It made her dislike the Caspian Sea
questions.why: Sitting at a seaside café, she realized the setback was exactly what she had needed, enjoying her new flexibility.

podcast.title: The job I almost quit

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Would you prefer to work from home or in an office? Guess: who in this episode wanted to resign from a job — Leyla or Sam?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is work and career — and I have a confession.
Go on.
In my first job, I almost decided to resign after six months. [sigh] My workload was crazy. I stayed at the office until nine every night.
Why so much?
I wanted to go the extra mile. I said yes to every task, every deadline. I thought that was the way to get a promotion.
And was it?
No! I was just tired and slow. My manager told me: doing more is not the same as doing better.
Wise manager. So what did you do?
I went back to the drawing board. I learned to say no politely, and to ask a colleague for help.
That's hard for many people. For me the big change was remote work.
Oh, you love working from home.
I do. No traffic, my own coffee, my cat. [chuckle] But sometimes I feel lonely.
Yes. In the office you chat at the coffee machine, you learn from people.
So now I go to the office two days a week. It's a good mix.
And what about your friend who started her own company?
Nigar! She's an entrepreneur now — she sells handmade bags online. She works hard, but she says she's never bored.
That's brave. Does she have any advice?
Yes: networking. Go to events, talk to people, help them. Most jobs come from people you know.
True. You don't have to climb the ladder alone. Other people can give you a hand.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is your dream job, and what is one step you can take towards it?
And remember — no one's dream job is staying at the office until nine! See you next time.
[laugh] Bye for now!
